series.name: Ego Down
series.tagline: Har rishte mein koi ek pehle jhukta hai.
series.concept: Pure scenes from couples, siblings, and friends — across the full arc of life (teens to 40s-50s). No characters, no narrator, no moral until the last slide. Each episode shows a precisely observed moment from a relationship, then drops the unwritten rule as the final punchline. The rule is the screenshot slide — the thing women DM to their sister, husband, or best friend.

episodes.title: Kya Khayega?

slides.text:
Episode 1

KYA KHAYEGA?

Saturday night.

She opens Swiggy.

"Bata, kya khayega?"

"Kuch bhi."

"Pizza?"
"Nahi."

"Chinese?"
"Abhi nahi."

"Butter chicken?"
"Heavy hai."

"Momos?"
"Kal khaye the."

"Toh TU bata na."

"Kuch bhi order kar de."

She stares at the screen.
Then closes Swiggy.

Opens Zomato.

Orders biryani.

He sees the notification.

"Oh, biryani? Nice."

She doesn't look up.

"Haan. Tera kuch bhi yehi tha."

The unwritten rule:

"Kuch bhi" ka matlab kabhi kuch bhi nahi hota.

Aur jisne ye samajh liya — usne poochna band kar diya.
Tag the one whose "kuch bhi" you've already decoded.

episodes.synopsis: Wife asks what to eat. Husband says kuch bhi. She suggests 4 things. All rejected. She orders what he wanted in the first place — without asking.
episodes.caption: Kitne saal lage tumhe "kuch bhi" decode karne mein? 😂

episodes.title: Wardrobe Partition

slides.text:
Episode 2

WARDROBE PARTITION

One wardrobe. Two sisters.

Left side: Didi's.
Right side: Chhoti's.

The line was drawn with a dupatta hanger.
Respected by neither.

"Mera white top kidhar hai?"
"Maine nahi liya."

It was under Chhoti's pillow.

Every. Single. Week.

Fights that shook the house.
Mamma screaming from the kitchen.
"EK AUR BAAR LADAI KI TOH DONO KE KAPDE BAHAR!"

Then Chhoti left for college.

The room got quieter.
The wardrobe got lighter.

Didi didn't celebrate the extra space.
She just closed the door softer.

Three years later. Chhoti visits.

Drops her bag. Opens the wardrobe.

Left side: full.
Right side: empty.

The dupatta hanger is still there.

The unwritten rule:

Woh jagah khali nahi chhodi kyunki bhool gayi.

Chhodi kyunki abhi bhi wait kar rahi hai ki tu aake ladegi.

Send this to your sister.
She'll know which side was hers.

episodes.synopsis: Two sisters sharing a room. Daily fights over borrowed clothes. Younger one moves out for college. Years later she visits. Her side of the wardrobe is still empty. Didi never expanded into it.
episodes.caption: Tumhari behen ka side abhi bhi khali hai? 🥲

episodes.title: Group Chat

slides.text:
Episode 3

GROUP CHAT

2015.

Five girls. One hostel floor.
One WhatsApp group: "Pagal Gang 🤪"

47 messages a day. Minimum.

2025.

Same group. New name: "College Wali Gang ❤️"

Last message:
"Happy Diwali everyone! 🪔"
— 4 months ago.

Sent by Priya. Liked by 2. Replied by 0.

Tuesday. 11:43 PM.

Priya opens the group.
Scrolls up. Old photos. Inside jokes.

She starts typing.

"Guys, March mein plan karte hain na?
Goa ya Udaipur?
Bahut ho gaya, milna chahiye."

Sent. ✓✓

Blue ticks. All five.

Wednesday. Thursday. Friday.

Nothing.

Saturday morning, Priya opens the chat.

Long press. Delete for everyone.

"This message was deleted."

The unwritten rule:

Group chat mein "plan karte hain" likhne wali jaanti hai koi nahi aayega.

Phir bhi likhti hai.

Apne group mein bhej.
Dekh kaun reply karta hai.

episodes.synopsis: 5 friends made a group in college. 10 years later. Last message: Happy Diwali — 4 months ago. One friend types 'guys plan karte hain.' Seen by all. Replied by none. She deletes the message.
episodes.caption: Tumhare group chat ka last message kab ka hai? Be honest. 😂

episodes.title: Goodnight

slides.text:
Episode 4

GOODNIGHT

2016.

2:17 AM.
Both still on the phone.

Neither has anything left to say.
But nobody hangs up.

"Okay, goodnight?"
"Hmm. Goodnight."

...

"So ja na."
"Tu pehle rakh."
"Nahi tu rakh."

Call duration: 3 hours 42 minutes.

Next morning.

"Kal kitne baje soye?"
"Pata nahi, call pe hi so gaye."

Both smiling.
Both exhausted.
Both doing it again tonight.

2024.

Same two people.

11:14 PM.

She's already asleep.
Phone on the pillow, screen still on.
Some reel playing on mute.

He picks up her phone.
Plugs it into the charger.
Switches off her side lamp.

Pulls the blanket up.

Doesn't say goodnight.
Doesn't need to.

She half-wakes.

"Soya nahi?"
"So ja."

She turns over.
Asleep in eight seconds.

The unwritten rule:

Pehle pyaar bolne mein tha.
Ab phone charge pe lagane mein hai.

Dono mein se koi chota nahi hai.
Send this to the one who still charges your phone at night.

episodes.synopsis: Before: 2 AM. Both on call. 'Tu rakh.' 'Nahi tu rakh.' Neither hangs up. After: Same couple, 8 years later. She's already asleep. He puts her phone on charge, switches off her side lamp.
episodes.caption: Phone charge pe lagana bhi pyaar hai. 🤍

episodes.title: Parents Ke Saamne

slides.text:
Episode 5

PARENTS KE SAAMNE

5:47 PM.

Bhai has the TV remote.
Behen wants to watch something else.

Negotiations have failed.
Diplomacy is over.

"De remote."
"Nahi."
"MUMMY KO BOLUGI."
"Bol. Mummy nahi hai."

Power confirmed.
Behen attacks.

Full contact combat.

Cushion thrown. Hair pulled. One chappal launched.
Remote now under the sofa.

"TU MARA HUA HAI AAJSE."
"TU PEHLE SE MARI HUI HAI."

Doorbell.

Both freeze.

"Papa."

0.3 seconds. That's all it takes.

Papa walks in.

Bhai: watching news. Posture: responsible.
Behen: scrolling phone. Expression: peaceful.

Cushion back in place.
Chappal on foot.
Remote casually on the armrest.

Bhai even offers: "Chai laaun?"

The unwritten rule:

Ghar mein sabse bada alliance parents ke saamne hota hai.

Koi nahi sikhaata — par dono ko pata hota hai.

Tag your bhai/behen.
They'll deny everything.

episodes.synopsis: Brother and sister fighting viciously. Doorbell — Papa home. Instant ceasefire. Both on the sofa, watching TV like nothing happened. Bhai even passes the remote.
episodes.caption: Tumhare ghar mein ceasefire kitne second mein hoti thi? 😂

episodes.title: Woh Nahi Bolti Ab

slides.text:
Episode 6

WOH NAHI BOLTI AB

She used to come home and talk.

For an hour. Sometimes more.

Office politics. The auto driver who overcharged.
What Priya wore. What Vikram said in the meeting.

He'd listen.

Sort of.

Phone in hand. Eyes on the screen.
"Hmm." "Haan." "Achha."

Present enough to answer. Not enough to remember.

Then one day she just... stopped.

Came home. Made chai. Sat beside him.
Watched whatever he was watching.

No stories. No office updates. Nothing.

He didn't notice.

Day one. Day three. Day seven.

Still didn't notice.

Or maybe he did. But thought: finally, some peace.

Day nine.

He put down his phone.

"Aaj kya hua office mein?"

She looked up. Surprised.

"Kuch nahi. Usual."

And went back to her phone.

The unwritten rule:

Jab tak woh bolti thi, tujhe lagta tha boring hai.

Ab jab nahi bolti — tujhe lagta hai kuch chhoot raha hai.

Woh window band ho gayi. Tujhe pata bhi nahi chala.
Send this to someone before they stop telling you things.

episodes.synopsis: She used to tell him everything — office gossip, the rude auto driver, what she had for lunch. He'd half-listen, scrolling his phone. One day she stops. He doesn't notice for a week. Then he does.
episodes.caption: Kabhi notice kiya ki unhone batana kab band kiya? 🥲

episodes.title: Birthday Budget

slides.text:
Episode 7

BIRTHDAY BUDGET

Group chat. Three people. One mission.
(Ananya not added. It's her birthday.)

Group name: "Ananya ka surprise 🎂"

Day 1. Plans: ambitious.

Priya: "Olive Garden? Only ₹2500 per head."
Riya: "Haan! And a cake from that French place."
Neha: "And a gift — I saw this perfume set, ₹3000."

Total planned: ₹8500.
Each one already calculating.

Day 3.

Priya: "Guys, Olive Garden is a bit... let's do somewhere chill?"
Riya: "Haan, ghar pe bana lete hain. More personal anyway."
Neha: "Totally. More special."

Olive Garden: cancelled. Budget: improving.

Day 5.

Neha: "That perfume is ₹3000... sab milke ek cheez lein?"
Priya: "Haan, ek nice gift milke — better than three small ones."
Riya: "Logical."

Perfume: not decided.
Gift budget: being negotiated.

Day of the birthday.

Riya shows up with a ₹200 chocolate cake.
"I made the icing myself."

One shared gift: a ₹600 photo frame.
Four photos printed inside. All of them together.

Ananya bursts into tears. Happy ones.

The unwritten rule:

Asli birthday surprise ye nahi ki kitna kharch kiya.

Ye hai ki char logon ne ek group bana liya — bina tere — tere liye.
Tag the friend who'd show up with a ₹200 cake and make it feel like the best birthday ever.

episodes.synopsis: Three friends plan a birthday surprise for the fourth. Fancy plans in the group chat. The budget shrinks with every message. Day of: ₹200 cake, one shared gift, one very happy birthday girl.
episodes.caption: Budget gaya budget. Par woh aayi. Bas yehi kaafi hai. 🎂

episodes.title: Bada Bhai, Chhota Bhai

slides.text:
Episode 8

BADA BHAI, CHHOTA BHAI

Papa found out about the marks.

The lecture lasted twelve minutes.
It felt like forty.

Bada bhai walked to his room.
Closed the door.

Not slammed. Just... closed.

Five minutes later.

Knock. Door opens.

Chhota bhai. Twelve years old.
Carrying nothing except his phone.

He doesn't say anything.
Just walks in.

Sits on the bed.

Opens his game.

Doesn't make eye contact.
Doesn't acknowledge the scolding happened.
Doesn't ask "kya hua."

Just... sits there.

Ten minutes.

Bada bhai stares at the ceiling.

Chhota bhai taps his screen.
Game sounds. Occasional sigh.

Neither speaks.
Neither needs to.

Twenty minutes later.

Bada bhai sits up.

"Chal, ice cream khate hain."

Chhota bhai doesn't look up.

"Chal."

The unwritten rule:

Chhota bhai kabhi nahi poochta "kya hua."

Bas aa jaata hai.

Uss kamre mein hona hi uska poochna hai.

Tag your bhai.
No explanation needed — he'll know.

episodes.synopsis: Older brother gets scolded by Papa. Goes to his room. Five minutes later, younger brother just appears — sits on the bed, plays on his phone. Doesn't say a word. Twenty minutes of silence. Then: 'Chal, ice cream khate hain.'
episodes.caption: Kuch poochha nahi. Bas aa gaya. Wahi kaafi tha. 🍦

episodes.title: The Driver's Seat

slides.text:
Episode 9

THE DRIVER'S SEAT

2014.

He always drove.

She always took the aux.

This was the arrangement. Unspoken. Absolute.

Her playlist: Bollywood. Loud. Emotional.

Him: "Yaar, kuch aur chala na."
Her: "Nahi. This is a classic."

Him: *sighs* *drives*

Two minutes later: humming along.

"Are you humming?"
"Nahi."
"You literally are."
"The song is stuck. Not my fault."

She turns up the volume.

He hums louder. Denies everything.

2024.

She drives now.

He's in the passenger seat.
Seat reclined. Eyes closed.

Her playlist: same Bollywood. Same songs. Ten years older.

She glances over.

He's asleep.

Or almost asleep.

His lips are moving.

Humming.

In his sleep.

Same song he complained about in 2014.

The unwritten rule:

Driver's seat badal gayi. Playlist nahi badli.

Kuch cheezein negotiate nahi hoti — settle ho jaati hain.
Tag the one who claims to hate your playlist — but knows every word.

episodes.synopsis: Before: He always drives. She controls the music. He pretends to hate her songs — but hums along. After: She's driving now. He's asleep in the passenger seat. Her playlist is still playing. He's still humming.
episodes.caption: Tum complain karte ho. Par gaana yaad hai tumhe. 😂

episodes.title: Mummy Ka Phone

slides.text:
Episode 10

MUMMY KA PHONE

Two siblings.

Didi moved to Bangalore five years ago.
Chhoti is still home. Same city. Twenty minutes away.

Mummy calls Didi every day.
Sometimes twice.

Chhoti once asked:
"Mummy, tujhe mujhe kyun nahi karti itna?"

Mummy: "Tu toh yahan hai. Milte rehte hain."

But they don't.

Not really.

Sunday.

Chhoti drops by.
No call ahead. Like the old days.

Doorbell. Mummy opens the door.

Phone to her ear. Hand up — one minute.

She's talking to Didi. Laughing.

Chhoti goes to the kitchen.

Boils water.
Measures tea leaves.
Adds ginger.

Mummy is still on the call.
Still laughing.

She can hear her telling Didi about the neighbour's son.

Twenty minutes.

Mummy walks into the kitchen.
Phone back in her pocket.

"Arey beta, tu kab aaya?"

Chhoti slides the chai across.

"Baith. Pee."

The unwritten rule:

Door wale ko phone milta hai.
Paas wale ko "tu toh hai hi" milta hai.

Dono ko lagta hai doosre ko zyada pyaar milta hai.

Dono galat hain. Dono sahi hain.

Send this to your sibling.
Door wala ya paas wala — dono samjhenge.

episodes.synopsis: One sibling lives far away; Mummy calls them every day. The other lives nearby — 'Tu toh yahan hai.' But they don't really meet. Near sibling drops by. Mummy is on a call with the far one, laughing. Near sibling makes chai and waits.
episodes.caption: "Tu toh hai hi" — sabse pyaara. Aur kabhi kabhi sabse dard dene wala bhi. 🥲

episodes.title: Seen Zone

slides.text:
Episode 11

SEEN ZONE

3:47 PM.

She types.
And types.
And types.

247 words.
About her day, her boss, her problem, and the thing she needs his help with.

Send.

Blue ticks.

4:02 PM: seen.

She puts her phone down.
Picks it up again.

4:30 PM: nothing.
5:15 PM: nothing.
6:00 PM: nothing.

6:15 PM.

She types: "?"

One character.
Sends it.

Blue ticks immediately.

"Haan padha. Soch raha tha."

She stares at the screen.

India v/s Australia was on since 1 PM.

He's been watching cricket for five hours.

What she doesn't know:

He did read it. Twice.

He just didn't know what to say.
So he said nothing.

Because nothing felt better than the wrong thing.

The unwritten rule:

Ladke ke liye seen = "soch raha hoon."
Ladki ke liye seen = "tujhe farak nahi padta."

Dono sach hai.
Aur dono akele feel karte hain.
Send this to the one who's been 'soch raha tha' since yesterday.

episodes.synopsis: She sends him a long message about her day, a work problem, asking for advice. Blue ticks. One hour. Two hours. She sends '?'. He replies: 'Haan padha. Soch raha tha.' He was watching cricket. But he did read it. Twice. He just didn't know what to say.
episodes.caption: "Soch raha tha" — 2 ghante. Kya soch raha tha? Cricket score? 😭

episodes.title: The Shaadi Shopping

slides.text:
Episode 12

THE SHAADI SHOPPING

Didi ki shaadi. Two months away.

Chhoti behen: self-appointed shopping commander.

Spreadsheet: open.
Budget: allocated.
Mission: nothing will go wrong.

Week 1: Four markets for the right dupatta shade.
Week 2: Argued with the jeweller for forty minutes.
Week 3: Returned the blouse twice. Wrong border.

Didi's lehenga: perfect.
Chhoti's shoes: worn out.

Three days before the wedding.

Didi pulls her aside.

"Tu bhi kuch le le apne liye.

Chal saath chalte hain."

Chhoti: "Nahi, sab ho gaya. Tujhe aur kuch chahiye?"

Didi: "Mujhe nahi. Tujhe."

Chhoti shakes her head.

"Phir kabhi."

Two words she's said her whole life.
For herself. Always later. Never now.

Wedding day.

Didi: flawless.
Chhoti: a suit from two years ago.

No one notices.

Except didi.

In one photo — didi is looking at chhoti.
Not the camera.

The unwritten rule:

Shaadi mein sabse zyada bhaagne wali apne liye kuch nahi laati.

Aur jis din uski shaadi hogi —
koi uske liye nahi bhaagega utna.

Sirf ek hogi. Woh wali didi.

Send this to your chhoti behen.
Woh jaanti hai kaun hai woh.

episodes.synopsis: Badi behen ki shaadi. Chhoti behen in charge of shopping. Runs across the city for matching dupattas, jewelry, shoes. Makes spreadsheets. Fights with vendors. The week before the wedding, didi says 'Tu bhi kuch le le apne liye.' Chhoti shakes her head. Didi's outfit is perfect. Chhoti wears something from last year. Nobody notices. Except didi.
episodes.caption: Sabke liye sab kuch. Apne liye "phir kabhi." 🥹

episodes.title: Last Bench, Last Time

slides.text:
Episode 13

LAST BENCH, LAST TIME

Class 10. Last bench. Four of them.

Unspoken rule: this is our territory.
Teachers knew. Tried anyway. Gave up.

Folded notes passed across three desks.
Tiffin box opened at 9 AM. Empty by 10.
One earphone each — left bud, right bud.

The music was terrible. Didn't matter.

Last period: always bunked.
Destination: the golgappe wala around the corner.

He knew their names.
He never charged them full price.

Those were the best golgappe in the world.

Ten years later.

Priya posts a school photo on Instagram.
"Found this 😭 #throwback"

Three likes. One within minutes.
One the next morning.
One four days later.

Tanya comments:
"Miss those days 😭"

Three heart reactions.
No replies.

Nobody DMs.
Nobody calls.

The golgappe wala is still there.
Same corner. Same cart.

He might still remember their names.

They're not.

The unwritten rule:

Last bench ki dosti mein koi promise nahi tha ki hamesha rahenge.

Isliye jab tak the — poora the.

Aur shayad isliye yaad bhi utna aata hai.

Tag your last bench wala dost.
Aaj baat karo. Instagram like nahi.

episodes.synopsis: Before: Four friends, last bench. Passing notes. Getting caught. Sharing tiffin. One earphone each. Bunking the last period. After: Ten years. One of them posts a school photo on Instagram. The others like it. One comments 'miss those days.' Nobody DMs. Nobody calls.
episodes.caption: "Miss those days 😭" — aur phir koi nahi bola kuch. Sab jaante hain yeh feeling. 🥲

episodes.title: AC Ka Temperature

slides.text:
Episode 14

AC KA TEMPERATURE

Every night. Same time. Same argument.

Him: "18 degree."
Her: "Are you trying to freeze me?"
Him: "Are you trying to boil me?"

This has been happening since 2019.

Tonight's negotiation:

Him: "20. Final."
Her: "Fine."

She does not think 20 is fine.

11:30 PM.

Him: shirtless, one foot outside the blanket, already asleep.

Her: blanket. Shawl on top of blanket. Socks.

War declared. Casualties: one warm person.

3:12 AM.

She wakes up. Reaches for the remote.

Very slowly.
Very quietly.

24°.

Back under the shawl. Satisfied.

5:04 AM.

He stirs. Opens one eye.
Reaches for the remote.

Very slowly.
Very quietly.

18°.

Rolls over. Asleep in thirty seconds.

The unwritten rule:

AC ka remote ghar ka sabse powerful weapon hai.

Aur isse koi jeetega nahi —
sirf turns lega.

Har raat. Bina bole. Hamesha.
Tag the one who "compromised" on 20° — and immediately changed it at 3 AM.

episodes.synopsis: Every night, the same war. He wants 18°. She wants 24°. He sets it to 20° as a compromise. She adds a blanket, a shawl, and socks. He's sleeping shirtless. At 3 AM, she quietly changes it to 24°. At 5 AM, he quietly changes it back. Neither acknowledges this.
episodes.caption: 18 ya 24? Yeh question nahi hai — yeh ghar ka constitution hai. ❄️🔥

episodes.title: Rakhi Ke Baad

slides.text:
Episode 15

RAKHI KE BAAD

Bhai lives in Pune. Comes home once a year.

For Rakhi.

Mummy starts cooking three days before.
His favourite: dal makhani, shahi paneer, and that halwa no one else makes right.

He arrives Friday evening.

Big welcome. Loud house.
Papa asking about work.
Mummy serving before anyone asks.
Behen teasing him about the weight he's gained.

"Pune mein khaana hi khaata hai kya?"

Saturday morning. Rakhi.

Thali ready. Roli, rice, diya.
Behen ties it — carefully, the way she always does.

He looks away. Eyes doing that thing.

He gives her the envelope. "Thoda zyada diya is baar."

She doesn't open it. "Pehle chai pi."

Family photos. Too many.

Mummy insisting on one more.
Papa adjusting his collar for every shot.

Then lunch. Then TV. Then silence.

Then him: "Subah ki train hai. Jaldi nikalna padega."

He leaves Sunday morning. 6 AM.

The house goes quiet.

Behen goes to the puja room.
Removes the thali.
Washes it slowly.
Dries it.
Puts it back on the shelf.

Won't touch it for a year.

The unwritten rule:

Rakhi ek din ki nahi hoti.

Rakhi ke baad ka silence —
woh asli distance hai.

Aur dono jaante hain. Dono chup rehte hain.

Send this to your bhai.
Bas is liye ki "reach ho gaya?" ke baad bhi baat karo.

episodes.synopsis: Bhai lives in another city. Comes home for Rakhi. Big welcome. Favourite food. Behen ties the rakhi. He gives the gift. Family photos. He leaves the next morning. The house goes quiet. Behen removes the thali. Washes it. Puts it back on the shelf. That night she texts: 'Reach ho gaya?' He replies: 'Haan.' Nothing for two weeks.
episodes.caption: "Reach ho gaya?" "Haan." Phir do hafte khamoshi. Yeh dono jaante hain. 🥲

episodes.title: Photo Mein Jagah

slides.text:
Episode 16

PHOTO MEIN JAGAH

Every family photo is a project.

She starts 15 minutes before.

Ootfit check. Hair check. Lighting check.
"Yahan nahi — wahan. Natural light zyada aata hai."

He wears whatever he's wearing.

No preparation. No mirror check.

"Ready hoon."

He has been ready for 14 minutes.

She positions them.
Adjusts the angle.
Hands the phone to someone.

"Thoda side se lo. Nahi — aur side se."

Click.

17 shots.

Review begins.

"Isme mera face weird hai."
"Isme tera acha hai par mera nahi."
"Isme dono aache hain par background..."

Retake.

He smiles the same smile in all 17 photos.

Same smile. Same eyes. Same angle.

He does not understand what "weird face" means.

All 17 photos look identical to him.

The unwritten rule:

Woh 17 photos isliye leti hai kyunki ek mein sab perfect aana chahiye.

Usse tera smile same hai — ye nahi pata.
Usse ye pata hai — ye woh photo hogi jo years baad dekhegi.

Aur tab bhi woh wohi sochegi: "Mera face thoda.."
Tag the one who approves photo 17 after rejecting photos 1-16 — and looks exactly the same in all of them.

episodes.synopsis: Every family photo. She spends 15 minutes getting ready, positions them, takes 17 shots, reviews all of them, retakes. He stands there, smiling the same smile in all 17 photos. She picks the one where she looks best. He looks the same in every single one.
episodes.caption: 17 photos. Woh har ek mein different dikhti hai. Woh har ek mein same dikhta hai. Phir bhi woh choose karti hai. 📸

episodes.title: Bade Ho Gaye

slides.text:
Episode 17

BADE HO GAYE

BEFORE.

Bada bhai comes home from college.

Chhota hears the door.
Drops whatever he's doing.
Runs.

Jumps on him.
Literally jumps.

Bada bhai drops his bag.
Wrestling match begins in the living room.

Mummy screaming from the kitchen:
"Dono pagal ho gaye hain!"

Bada bhai pins him.
Chhota protests.
"Cheating hai!"

Bada bhai lets him win.
Chhota knows.
Neither says anything.

AFTER.

Same brothers. Three years later.

Bada bhai visits.
Chhota opens the door.

They look at each other.

Handshake.
Then a hug — but a quick one.

Both pat each other's back.
Exactly twice.

They come inside.
Sit.
Talk about work.

Nobody wrestles.

Bada bhai leaves.

Chhota stands at the balcony.
Watches.

Until the cab disappears around the corner.

The unwritten rule:

Bade ho gaye ka matlab ye nahi ki pyaar kam ho gaya.

Matalab ye hai ki ab dikhane mein sharam aati hai.

Woh balcony se dekhna —
wohi bachpan wala door tak bhaagna hai.

Apne bhai ko bhejo.
Kuch mat likho.
Bas bhejo.

episodes.synopsis: Two brothers. Before: Bada bhai returns from college, chhota jumps on him, wrestling match in the living room. After: Same brothers, years later. Handshake. Quick hug. Two pats. They sit. They talk about work. Nobody wrestles. But chhota stands at the balcony and watches the cab until it disappears.
episodes.caption: Handshake. Do pat. Work ki baatein. Aur phir balcony se cab jaate dekha. Bade ho gaye. 🥲

episodes.title: Sorry Pehle

slides.text:
Episode 18

SORRY PEHLE

Ladai hui.

Koi badi wajah nahi thi.
Ya thi — but neither can remember it now.

Dono angry. Dono silent.

She: bedroom. Phone.
He: hall. Phone.

Same house. Different rooms.
Same thought:

"Woh pehle aayega/aayegi."

2 hours pass.
4 hours pass.

Hunger arrives.
Neither acknowledges hunger.

Hunger leaves, embarrassed.

10 PM.

He gets up.
Goes to the kitchen.

Kettle on.
Two cups.
Two tea bags.

Measures milk like he always does.

Walks to the bedroom.

Places one cup on her bedside table.

Doesn't say sorry.
Doesn't say anything.

Walks back to the hall.

The unwritten rule:

Sorry bolna zaroori nahi hota.

Chai rakh dena — wohi sorry hai.

Aur dono ko pata hai.
Aur ladai khatam ho gayi.
Kisi ne announce nahi kiya.

Tag the one who says sorry with chai instead of words.

Woh sahi hai, by the way.

episodes.synopsis: A fight. Both silent. Cold war for hours. She's in the bedroom, he's in the hall. Both waiting for the other to apologize first. At 10 PM he goes to the kitchen, makes two cups of chai, places one on her bedside table. Walks out. Doesn't say sorry. She picks up the cup. The fight is over.
episodes.caption: Koi sorry nahi bola. Chai aa gayi. Ladai khatam. Yeh couple therapy se sasta aur acha hai. ☕

episodes.title: Plus One

slides.text:
Episode 19

PLUS ONE

Teen purani dost. Ek wedding.

Dono shaadi-shuda hain.
Ek nahi.

Sabne ek hi car mein aaya. Teen WhatsApp groups mein saath hain. Sab theek hai.

Conversation at the table:

"Bete ki school admission process shuru karo abhi se."
"EMI se bohot pressure hai yaar."
"In-laws ka scene toh poochh mat."

Single friend nods.
Sips her drink.

Dance floor.

Single friend: "Chalo!"

Dono married friends:
"Nahi yaar. Thak gayi hoon."
"Back mein dard hai."

Both are 29.

She dances anyway.

Alone-ish.
With the dulhe ke cousins she doesn't know.

She looks back once at her friends.

They're checking their phones.

Drive back. 1 AM.

One married friend, half-asleep:
"Yaar... tu mat badalna."

Single friend smiles.
"Haan yaar."

She doesn't say what she's thinking.

The unwritten rule:

Shaadi ke baad dosti khatam nahi hoti.

Bas ek ko lagta hai doosra badal gaya.

Dono sahi hain.
Dono thoda akela feel karta hai.
Dono bol nahi sakte.

Woh purani dost — jo EMI waali hai ya dance floor waali — dono ko bhejo.

Bas taki pata chale.

episodes.synopsis: Three friends at a wedding. Two are married. Conversations have shifted to school admissions and EMIs. Single friend nods along. Married friends sit out the dance floor. Single friend dances alone. On the drive back, one says 'Yaar, tu mat badalna.' Single friend laughs. Doesn't say: 'Tu badal gayi.'
episodes.caption: "Tu mat badalna" — woh boli. Usne socha: "Tu badal gayi." Dono sahi thi. 💛

episodes.title: Ghar Aa Ja

slides.text:
Episode 20

GHAR AA JA

Long distance.

He's working in another city.
She's here.

Weekend calls. Week mein teen-chaar messages.
Sab theek hai. Sab adjust kar liya.

Tuesday. 10:30 PM. She calls.

He picks up.
"Haan bolo."

She doesn't say what she wants to say.

She says: "Bijli ka bill aaya hai."

He: "Kitna aaya?"
She: "Zyada. 2400."
He: "Pay kar dena. Main amount bhejta hoon."

Then: "Aur?"

She: "Washing machine mein awaaz aa rahi hai."

He knows.

He gives the practical answer first:
"Mechanic ko bulao. Main number dhundta hoon."

Then a pause.

"Bahut awaaz aa rahi hai?"

She: "Haan."

Neither of them is talking about the washing machine.

He: "Aaja next weekend? Main ticket bhejta hoon."

She: "Dekhti hoon."

The unwritten rule:

Jab bolti hai 'bijli ka bill aaya' —
woh ye keh rahi hai 'ghar aa ja.'

Aur jab woh 'dekhti hoon' bolti hai —
ticket book ho chuka hai.

Usse bhejo jo door hai.
Bas isiliye.

episodes.synopsis: Long-distance couple. She calls. Says practical things — bijli ka bill, washing machine mein awaaz. He answers practically. Then a pause. 'Bahut awaaz aa rahi hai?' She says yes. He knows she's not talking about the washing machine. 'Aaja next weekend?' 'Dekhti hoon.' Ticket already booked.
episodes.caption: "Bijli ka bill aaya." Matlab: ghar aa ja. Long distance mein sirf dil nahi translate karta — poori bhaasha badal jaati hai. 🏡

episodes.title: Tere Bina Plan

slides.text:
Episode 21

TERE BINA PLAN

College. 2015.

"Agar tu nahi aa rahi toh main bhi cancel."

Every time. Every plan.

Her presence was the plan.

Plans made in 10 minutes.
Cancelled in 2.
Made again in 5.

No WhatsApp group needed.

Just: "Aa rahi hai?"
"Haan. Kab?"

They went everywhere together.
And nowhere specifically.

That was the point.

The destination was always: tere saath.

Now. 2024.

Same two friends.

One has a baby.
Plans: 3 weeks advance notice.
Cancelled: 2 hours before.

"Next time pakka."

Both know 'next time' is next time.

Not a lie.
Not a promise.

Just what you say
when life has become
bigger than a plan.

One day —
the friend without kids
stops asking.

Not out of anger.
Out of understanding.

And that's
the saddest kind of love.

The unwritten rule:

Tere bina plan nahi tha — woh wala time chala gaya.

Ab plan bina tere banta hai.
Aur dono ko dukh hai —
par koi nahi bolta.

Woh dost — jo samajhti hai par poochh nahi sakti — usse bhejo.

Woh jaanti hai kyon.

episodes.synopsis: Before: every plan in college revolved around her presence. After: same two friends, different lives. One has a baby now. Plans are scheduled 3 weeks ahead and cancelled 2 hours before. One day the friend without kids quietly stops asking — not out of anger, but out of understanding.
episodes.caption: "Agar tu nahi aa rahi toh main bhi cancel." Woh wala time ab woh wala time nahi raha. Dono jaante hain. Dono nahi bolte. 🤍

episodes.title: Bathroom Ka Time

slides.text:
Episode 22

BATHROOM KA TIME

Morning routine.
6 years of marriage.

She needs: 45 minutes.
He needs: 10.

This is a known fact.
By both parties.

7:00 AM. She goes in.

He makes chai.
Scrolls phone.
Waits.

7:20 AM. He knocks.

"Kitna time aur?"

Her, from inside:

"Bas 5 minute."

He knows this means 25.
She knows he knows.

Neither of them changes anything.

7:45 AM. She comes out.

Fresh. Ready. Perfectly.

He rushes in.
Uses exactly 8 minutes.

Out by 7:53.

In 6 years —

Neither has suggested a schedule.
Neither has proposed a solution.
Neither has downloaded a bathroom timer app.

This is the system.

The unwritten rule:

Bathroom ka '5 minute' aur
food delivery ka '30 minute' —
dono ka sach dono ko pata hai.

Par poochna aur bolna
band nahi hota.

Yeh bhi pyaar hai.

Us insaan ko bhejo
jo '5 minute' bol ke 25 lete hain.

Woh jaanta hai.

episodes.synopsis: She needs 45 minutes in the bathroom. He needs 10. Every morning: she goes in, he knocks at 7:20, she says '5 minute', he waits 25 more. Both know the script. Neither changes it. They've been doing this for 6 years.
episodes.caption: "Bas 5 minute." 6 saal baad bhi same answer. Same wait. Same system. 🚿 Kaun hai tere ghar mein?

episodes.title: Teri Shaadi Mein

slides.text:
Episode 23

TERI SHAADI MEIN

Chhoti behen ki shaadi.

Badi behen has:
— Finalized the venue.
— Chosen the lehenga.
— Approved the mehendi design.

Chhoti behen has:
— Been consulted. Technically.

Chhoti wanted: garden venue.
Badi booked: banquet hall.

Chhoti wanted: simple lehenga.
Badi chose: 9-kilo heavily embroidered.

Chhoti wanted: minimal mehendi.
Badi got: full arms, both sides.

Chhoti, frustrated:
"YAAR. Yeh MERI shaadi hai!"

Badi, unbothered:
"Haan haan. Tu pehli baar kar rahi hai.
Tujhe kya pata kya accha lagta hai."

Chhoti: 😤

Shaadi ka din.

Chhoti walks into the venue.

The lights. The flowers.
The exact warmth she would've wanted
if she'd known what she wanted.

She sees herself in the mirror.
The lehenga. The mehendi.

She looks...
beautiful.

More beautiful than she planned.

She will not say this out loud.
Not today. Not ever. Not for 10 years.

The unwritten rule:

Badi behen ko control freak mat bol.

Usse tera taste
tujhse better pata hai.

Aur tujhe bhi —
bas accept karne mein ego aata hai.

Apni badi behen ko bhejo.
Bina kuch bole.

Woh samjhegi.

episodes.synopsis: Chhoti behen's shaadi. Badi behen has taken over every decision — venue, lehenga, mehendi. Chhoti is furious. Then on the wedding day she sees how perfectly everything turned out. She won't admit this for 10 years.
episodes.caption: "Yeh MERI shaadi hai!" Haan. Aur badi behen ne isko exactly waisa banaya jaise hona chahiye tha. 10 saal baad maanegi. 💍

episodes.title: Read Receipts Off

slides.text:
Episode 24

READ RECEIPTS OFF

4 months ago.
She turned off read receipts.

He noticed.
He didn't say anything.

Now:

When she doesn't reply —
he can't tell if she's seen it.

So he checks her last seen.
"2 minutes ago."

Message: single tick.

He knows she saw it.

She knows he checked.

Neither brings it up.

4 months of this.

One night.

She's texting her friend about him.

"Usne phir se last seen check kiya 😂"

She presses send.

Wrong chat.

He sees it.

She deletes it.

Too late.

They make eye contact.

Both look away.

Neither says a word.

The unwritten rule:

Read receipts off karna ek decision hai.
Last seen check karna ek habit hai.

Dono jaante hain doosra kya kar raha hai.

Koi nahi rokta.
Koi nahi poochta.

Yeh bhi relationship hai.

Us insaan ko bhejo
jiske read receipts off hain.

Woh jaanta hai kyon.

episodes.synopsis: She turned off read receipts. He noticed. Now he checks her last seen instead. She knows. He knows she knows. Four months of this silent standoff — until she accidentally forwards a message about him to him.
episodes.caption: Read receipts off. Last seen: 2 minute pehle. Single tick. Dono jaante hain. Koi nahi bolta. 📱 Sound familiar?

episodes.title: Ego Down

slides.text:
Episode 25

EGO DOWN

50s. Kids grown. Gone.

Empty house.

They've run out of things
to fight about.

That took 28 years.

One evening.

She's watching TV.

He walks in with two plates.
Dinner he made.
Nothing fancy.

Dal chawal.

She looks at the plate.

Takes one bite.

"Namak kam hai."

He takes the plate back.

Goes to the kitchen.

Adds namak.

Brings it again.

No comment. No face.

She takes a bite.

"Ab theek hai."

They eat in silence.

Not cold silence.

The kind where you don't need
to perform anymore.

The unwritten rule:

Ego down ka matlab ye nahi ki haar gayi.

Matalab ye hai ki rishta
usse zyada important hai
jitna sahi hona.

25 episode dekh liye.
Ab apna ego down kar.

Yeh last episode hai.

Episode 1 uss insaan ko bhej
jo tere liye ego down karta hai.

Har baar.

episodes.synopsis: An older couple in their 50s. Kids are grown and gone. Empty house. They've run out of things to fight about. One evening he makes dal chawal without being asked. She says 'namak kam hai.' He adds namak. She takes a bite. 'Ab theek hai.' They eat in silence — not cold silence. The kind where you don't need to perform.
episodes.caption: 28 saal. Empty house. Dal chawal. "Namak kam hai." He added namak. No argument. Bas itna. Ego down. 🍚
